summary: South Africa's deputy president Jacob Zuma was repeatedly named in corruption charges against his financial adviser Schabir Shaik, though Zuma himself was not charged.

Former financial adviser Schabir Shaik was found guilty of corruption in a verdict that implicated South African Deputy President Jacob Zuma, prompting calls for Zuma's resignation and a no-confidence motion.
The corruption trial of former South African deputy president Jacob Zuma was postponed until November 12 while hundreds of supporters cheered him outside Durban magistrates' court.
South Africa's former deputy president Jacob Zuma was indicted on corruption charges, including accepting bribes from French arms firms, which he denies.
Jacob Zuma confirmed that he was being investigated for rape, an allegation he denies.
South Africa's ruling African National Congress suspended its deputy leader, Jacob Zuma, pending his trial for rape.
Jacob Zuma's rape trial opened in Johannesburg, where he denied the charge, and the presiding judge stepped down after his lawyers argued impartiality was in question.

The rape trial of former South African deputy president Jacob Zuma was postponed after defence lawyers objected to the appointment of Judge Jeremiah Shongwe, reportedly because his sister had an affair with Zuma three decades ago that produced a son.

The rape trial of South Africa's sacked deputy president Jacob Zuma began with graphic testimony from a sobbing HIV-positive Aids activist who claimed she was forced to have sex with him against her will, while Zuma pleaded not guilty.
A verdict is expected in the rape trial of former South African deputy president Jacob Zuma, with the case determining whether he can pursue his ambition to succeed Thabo Mbeki as president in 2009.
Jacob Zuma was acquitted of rape charges and announced he would resume his political career, posing a challenge to President Thabo Mbeki.
Jacob Zuma was reinstated as deputy president of South Africa's ruling African National Congress.
Jacob Zuma was acquitted of raping a friend's daughter.
Former South African deputy president Jacob Zuma sues leading newspapers and radio stations for 63 million rand, claiming their coverage of his recent rape trial was defamatory and biased.
Former South African deputy president Jacob Zuma sues leading newspapers and radio stations for 63 million rand, claiming their coverage of his recent rape trial was defamatory and biased.
The corruption trial of Jacob Zuma was postponed until September as about 5,000 supporters gathered outside Pietermaritzburg high court.
A South African judge dismissed corruption charges against former deputy president Jacob Zuma, freeing him to pursue a campaign to become the next president.

A South African court of appeal ruled that the police seizure of allegedly incriminating documents from Jacob Zuma's home and office was legal, opening the way for him to be charged with corruption over a multi-billion dollar weapons deal.

Jacob Zuma is positioned to defeat Thabo Mbeki in the African National Congress leadership election at the party conference opening on Sunday, though a possible corruption prosecution could derail his presidential bid.
Jacob Zuma gained the upper hand in the ANC leadership battle as supporters jeered President Thabo Mbeki at the party conference, with a vote result expected the following day.
South Africa's ruling African National Congress elected Jacob Zuma as its new leader, defeating President Thabo Mbeki.
Jacob Zuma defeats Thabo Mbeki for control of the ANC, positioning himself for a shot at becoming South Africa's next president.

South Africa's director of public prosecutions said there is sufficient evidence to charge Jacob Zuma, the newly elected leader of the African National Congress, with corruption for allegedly accepting substantial bribes from a French arms company, with a final decision on when to charge him described as imminent.
Jacob Zuma makes his first address as leader of the ruling African National Congress.
Jacob Zuma, who recently defeated Thabo Mbeki to become African National Congress leader, was served with prosecution papers for alleged corruption, with a trial scheduled for 2008-08-14.
Jacob Zuma, newly elected president of South Africa's ruling African National Congress, announces he is to marry Nompumelo Ntuli as his fourth wife.
The ANC national executive committee decided that Jacob Zuma would lead the ANC's campaign in the 2009 elections, amid tensions over corruption charges and a split with Thabo Mbeki.

Jacob Zuma, elected ANC president in December 2007, faces ongoing disputes within his coalition, a cold war with President Mbeki, and uncertainty over future policies, while some supporters want him to depose Mbeki immediately.

Jacob Zuma, president-elect of the ANC, appears to be using his influence with South Africa's trade unions to break the deadlock in Zimbabwe, with the South African transport and allied workers union (Satawu) deciding not to unload a Chinese vessel carrying arms for the Zimbabwe government.
Jacob Zuma, president of South Africa's ruling ANC, described the delay in announcing Zimbabwe's election results as unacceptable and called for an African mission to Zimbabwe.
Jacob Zuma attended a formal celebration of Nelson Mandela's 90th birthday at Mandela's home in Qunu, Eastern Cape.
Jacob Zuma asked the high court to quash corruption charges against him.
Jacob Zuma appeared in court in Maritzburg to try to get corruption and fraud charges against him dropped, as more than 1,000 supporters rallied outside.
A South African judge reserved judgment until September 12 on Jacob Zuma's request to dismiss corruption charges against him.
A South African high court judge dismissed fraud and corruption charges against ANC leader Jacob Zuma on procedural grounds, ruling the prosecution appeared politically motivated.
A court found that President Thabo Mbeki influenced prosecutors to bring fraud and corruption charges against Jacob Zuma, and dismissed the case against Zuma.
Jacob Zuma was effectively cleared of corruption charges, taking a major step toward becoming South Africa's president.
Prosecutors said they would appeal against a judge's ruling dismissing fraud and corruption charges against Jacob Zuma, the president of the African National Congress.

South Africa's ruling African National Congress begins a meeting to decide whether to remove Thabo Mbeki as president after a high court judge accused him of misusing the justice system in a power struggle with Jacob Zuma.

The African National Congress begins a meeting to decide whether to remove Thabo Mbeki as South Africa's president after a high court judge accused Mbeki of misusing the justice system in a power struggle with Jacob Zuma.
Thabo Mbeki resigns as South Africa's president after being toppled by the ANC following a power struggle with former deputy Jacob Zuma.
South Africa's ruling African National Congress chose Kgalema Motlanthe, a close ally of Jacob Zuma, to replace Thabo Mbeki as president.

A third of South Africa's cabinet resigns amid a political crisis following the ANC's forced removal of President Thabo Mbeki, with Jacob Zuma facing calls to step aside as ANC leader to prevent a party split.
Kgalema Motlanthe was sworn in as South Africa's president, putting allies of Jacob Zuma firmly in control of the government after they toppled Thabo Mbeki.
A court reinstates corruption charges against Jacob Zuma.
Nelson Mandela made a rare appearance at an ANC rally in the Eastern Cape in support of party leader Jacob Zuma ahead of the April election.
South African prosecutors are reportedly poised to drop corruption charges against ANC leader Jacob Zuma, according to local media.
South African prosecutors dropped corruption charges against Jacob Zuma, clearing the way for him to potentially become president if the ANC wins the April 22 elections.
South African prosecutors dropped corruption charges against Jacob Zuma, clearing the way for him to become the country's next president after the 22 April elections.
Jacob Zuma agreed to suspend a plan to replace taxis with buses, yielding to taxi owners' demands ahead of the South African elections.
Jacob Zuma swept into power as South Africa's fourth post-apartheid president as the African National Congress was narrowly ahead of the two-thirds majority in vote counting.
Millions of South Africans voted in the country's most competitive election since the end of apartheid, with Jacob Zuma confident of becoming president as early results showed the ANC leading.
Jacob Zuma voted in South Africa's election in his rural Zulu homeland, with his youngest wife, Nompumelelo Ntuli, standing to the side.
The African National Congress, led by Jacob Zuma, leads South Africa's election with 67% of the vote, enough for a two-thirds majority.
Jacob Zuma claimed victory in the South African election, with the African National Congress taking 66.1% of the vote with around 95% of votes counted.
Jacob Zuma's ANC wins a mandate just short of a two-thirds majority in South Africa's elections, energizing the electorate and prompting challenges for his incoming leadership.
South Africa's parliament elected ANC leader Jacob Zuma as the country's fourth post-apartheid president.
Jacob Zuma is sworn in as president of South Africa.
Jacob Zuma, the new South African president, announced his first cabinet, sacking health minister Barbara Hogan and moving her to the public enterprises portfolio.
Jacob Zuma, the president of South Africa, married his third wife, Tobeka Madiba, in a traditional Zulu ceremony, during which he reportedly slipped and fell while performing a solo dance.
Jacob Zuma reportedly fathered his 20th child with Sonono Khoza, a woman who is not one of his three wives, prompting criticism that his behavior undermines the government's AIDS campaign.
Jacob Zuma apologises for fathering his 20th child with a woman who is not one of his three wives.
South African President Jacob Zuma called for international sanctions on Zimbabwe to be lifted during a state visit to the UK.
Jacob Zuma makes a state visit to the UK, meeting the Queen at Buckingham Palace and pressing Gordon Brown to lift EU and US sanctions on Robert Mugabe and his allies.

South African President Jacob Zuma attacked neocolonial British attitudes toward "barbaric" Africans at the outset of his most important foreign tour yet, amid revelations about his messy personal life.
A minister disclosed that the state had a 15.5 million rand budget for President Jacob Zuma's family this year, prompting opposition criticism and an ANC response.

Jacob Zuma led a recent state visit to Britain, where his large delegation and numerous fans prompted the reception to be held at the Dorchester hotel rather than the High Commission, and his speech praised the upcoming football rather than the heroic past.
Jacob Zuma is due to arrive in Tripoli with other African Union leaders to meet Muammar Gaddafi in a last-ditch attempt to broker a diplomatic end to the fighting in Libya.
South African civil rights groups condemn President Jacob Zuma's nomination of Justice Mogoeng Mogoeng for chief justice, citing his rulings on gender equality and marital rape.
South African President Jacob Zuma takes an artist and a gallery to court to have a painting depicting him with his genitals exposed removed, and the painting is defaced.
Jacob Zuma faces criticism and possible removal over his handling of the Marikana mine killings, in which 34 striking mineworkers were shot by police.
Eight opposition parties in South Africa tabled a motion of no confidence in President Jacob Zuma, an unprecedented move in the country's 18-year democratic history.
Kgalema Motlanthe confirms he will run against Jacob Zuma for the ANC presidency at the party's national conference in Mangaung.
Jacob Zuma won the African National Congress leadership election, defeating Kgalema Motlanthe by 2,983 votes to 991.
Jacob Zuma was re-elected as leader of the ANC, retaining his role as South African president and SADC facilitator of political reforms in Zimbabwe.

South Africa's main opposition party, the Democratic Alliance, announces Mamphela Ramphele as its presidential candidate to run against incumbent president Jacob Zuma in the upcoming national elections.

President Jacob Zuma predicts the African National Congress will win overwhelmingly in South Africa's general election and defends himself against corruption and Nkandla allegations at a final campaign media briefing.

South African President Jacob Zuma appointed Lynne Brown as the country's first openly gay cabinet minister, along with Nhlanhla Nene as the first black finance minister, as part of his new cabinet following his inauguration for a second term.
Jacob Zuma criticizes Oscar Pistorius's defence team for arguing that his disability and wealth should spare him prison, ahead of Pistorius's sentencing for culpable homicide.

South African President Jacob Zuma is under official investigation by the South African Human Rights Commission for hate speech after blaming the country's problems on the arrival of Dutch settler Jan van Riebeeck.
President Jacob Zuma announced that the official investigation report into the Marikana mine massacre will be released by the end of June.
South African police announce a corruption probe into President Jacob Zuma's son Duduzane and the Gupta family following a complaint by the opposition Democratic Alliance.

South Africa's constitutional court ruled that President Jacob Zuma failed to uphold the constitution by ignoring an order to repay government funds used for non-security upgrades to his private residence at Nkandla, and ordered him to repay the costs.
Anti-apartheid activist Ahmed Kathrada publicly called on President Jacob Zuma to resign over a scandal involving state spending on his private mansion.
South African President Jacob Zuma survived an impeachment vote in parliament after the African National Congress gave him its backing, though calls for him to step down continued.

South Africa's anti-corruption watchdog Thuli Madonsela publishes a report calling for a judicial inquiry into alleged influence-peddling involving President Jacob Zuma and his son, prompting intensified calls for his resignation.

South African President Jacob Zuma appeared to have survived an ANC national executive committee debate over whether he should resign, with aides saying he would leave for Fidel Castro's funeral as scheduled.
Three South African ministers called for President Jacob Zuma to resign at a weekend meeting of senior ANC officials.
South African President Jacob Zuma sacked finance minister Pravin Gordhan in an overnight cabinet purge, triggering a political crisis.
Tens of thousands of people marched across South Africa calling for Jacob Zuma to step down, amid scattered clashes and a second ratings agency downgrading the country to junk status.
Jacob Zuma faces renewed pressure to step down after media reports detailed links between elected officials and the Gupta family of tycoons accused of holding undue sway over his administration.
Opposition parties and critics in the ruling ANC prepare to mount a vote of no confidence in President Jacob Zuma in parliament, with a secret ballot possible after a June court ruling.
Jacob Zuma narrowly survives a motion of no confidence in South African parliament, with 198 MPs voting against and 177 in favour.
Jacob Zuma marries for the fifth time.
